blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre ética ambiental a partir de uma entrevista, usando substantivos abstratos e voz passiva, com ritmo adequado.

body: Esta aula treina **escrever frases claras e corretas (IELTS Writing, TOEFL Writing)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.intro: An environmental philosopher discusses whether nature has value in itself.
qa: Interviewer: Why does it matter whether nature has intrinsic value?

Because it **shapes what we owe** it. If value **is conferred only by human interest**, a forest is **protected** only when we **happen to want it**. **Aldo Leopold**, in *A Sand County Almanac* (1949), proposed a **land ethic**: a thing is right when it **tends to preserve** the **integrity** of the biotic community.
Interviewer: Isn’t that too abstract for policy?
Not entirely. **Rights of nature** statutes, **adopted in several places**, **grant legal standing** to rivers and ecosystems. **Whether** that is wise **remains debated**.
**Intergenerational justice** requires that the **options** we leave them **not be foreclosed**. **We are stewards**, not owners.

items.q: The philosopher thinks nature has value only when humans want it.
items.why: shapes what we owe… (she questions it).

items.q: Rights-of-nature laws exist in every country.

blocks.body: Discussões de ética usam **nomes abstratos** (*justice, integrity*) e **passiva** para deixar o agente implícito. Em fala, a ênfase marca o contraste: *STEWARDS, not OWNERS*.
*Environment* é substantivo; *environmental* é adjetivo: *environmental ethics* ✓, *environment ethics* ✗.

items.s: Value is ___ only by human interest. (confer)
Rights of nature statutes were ___ in several places. (adopt)

body: **Leave a legacy.** — Deixar um legado.
**Tread lightly.** — Pisar leve.
**Mother Nature.** — Mãe Natureza.
**Green with envy.** — Verde de inveja.
**The big picture.** — O panorama geral.
**Sustain the balance.** — Manter o equilíbrio.
**Pay the price.** — Pagar o preço.
**Time is running out.** — O tempo está acabando.
**For future generations.** — Para as futuras gerações.
**Drop in the ocean.** — Gota no oceano.
**Does nature have value in itself?** — A natureza tem valor em si mesma?
**And what do we owe the future?** — E o que devemos ao futuro?
**Options that are not foreclosed. We are stewards, not owners.** — Opções que não sejam bloqueadas. Somos administradores, não donos.

prompts.model: Rivers are granted legal standing in some places.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence reflection on our duties to future generations, using two abstract nouns, a passive and a not… but… contrast.
blocks.model: Justice between generations demands restraint. Options should not be foreclosed. The integrity of ecosystems is often treated as a luxury; it is, rather, a precondition. We are stewards, not owners. Whether our habits can change remains debated. The question, however, cannot be postponed.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
